rationale: Evidence from available literature on mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly defects and FDXR-associated disease indicates that while marked hyperglycinemia is a hallmark of MMDS1-3 due to direct impairment of lipoic acid cofactor synthesis required for the glycine cleavage system, glycine elevation in FDXR deficiency (MMDS9B) is inconsistent and not ubiquitous across the disease spectrum. Reports identifying elevated CSF and plasma glycine and lactate in FDXR deficiency originate primarily from severe early-onset cohorts, whereas broader systemic reviews and cohorts presenting predominantly with optic/acoustic neuropathy and sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy do not exhibit persistent or universal hyperglycinemia. However, exact age-stratified metabolic testing rates remain incompletely documented across all reported adult cases.

evidence.text: In FDXR deficiency, CSF lactate and to a milder extent plasma lactate was increased, which was also the case for CSF and plasma glycine in an early described cohort.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact sensitivity and specificity of plasma versus CSF glycine elevation across infantile versus juvenile/adult FDXR cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Direct retrospective quantification of CSF:plasma glycine ratios in all 44+ published FDXR patients stratified by age at onset would establish whether normal glycine metabolism definitively rules out infantile MMDS9B versus juvenile optic-acoustic neuropathy.
